hallucinations.claim: in the case of AWQ, also quantify activations
hallucinations.why: AWQ is weight-only (W4A16). It uses activation statistics to protect salient channels but does not quantize activations (arXiv 2306.00978)

hallucinations.claim: on an H100 the INT4 support can give a 2-3x throughput boost
hallucinations.why: Hopper (H100) tensor cores dropped INT4 support, which A100 had. 4-bit decode speedups come from cutting memory bandwidth (weights dequantized to fp16), not native INT4 compute

hallucinations.claim: Modern recipes (GPTQ, AWQ, QLoRA) run a quick calibration run on a small dataset
hallucinations.why: QLoRA's NF4 is calibration-free data-type quantization plus adapter fine-tuning; only GPTQ and AWQ calibrate

hallucinations.claim: The industry standard is *per-channel* scaling (each weight group shares a scale)
hallucinations.why: This conflates per-channel with per-group. The 4-bit standard is group-wise scaling (groups of 32-128 weights), which is finer than per-channel

hallucinations.claim: the drop can climb to 5-10 % for larger or very sensitive tasks
hallucinations.why: Gets the direction wrong: larger models are more robust to 4-bit, and losses grow for small (<3B) models, long reasoning, exact code/math and sub-4-bit schemes

hallucinations.claim: On a GPU that can natively pack INT4, the kernel can run a few times faster
hallucinations.why: Gets the mechanism wrong: the speedup comes from decoding being memory-bandwidth-bound (a quarter of the bytes read per token), which applies on any hardware, not from native INT4 packing

hallucinations.claim: ~6.5 GB in 4-bit, fitting on a single RTX 3090 or a dual-RTX 4090
hallucinations.why: A ~7 GB model fits on one 8-12 GB card, so citing a 24 GB 3090 or a 'dual-RTX 4090' is incoherent. Real 4-bit 13B files run ~7-8 GB once scales are included

hallucinations.claim: Running a 7-B Llama-2 on a single RTX 3090 in 4-bit is feasible
hallucinations.why: A 7B model already fits a 24 GB 3090 at fp16 (~14 GB), so the example shows nothing. Llama-2 is a stale 2023 example given without a date
Typical groups are 32-128 (MLX 64, GPTQ/AWQ 128, GGUF 32 within 256 super-blocks). Calling 256 a common block size is loose

hallucinations.claim: Smaller VRAM means fewer GPU hours, cutting cloud spend
hallucinations.why: A vague overclaim: VRAM footprint doesn't translate directly into GPU hours
